But how do systems like Redis handle that kind of location-based data so efficiently? That’s where Geospatial Indexes come into play. Geospatial indexes allow databases to store and query geographic data like longitude and latitude. In Redis, this capability is built right into the database—no external plugin or GIS system required. With geospatial indexes, you can: Store the location of items on a map Search for places nearby a given point Calculate distances between two coordinates This makes it useful for real-time applications like food delivery apps, fleet tracking, store locators, and more.
